sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5,931.4 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
Growth slowed from 64.2% in FY2021 to 0.1% in FY2023 and 10.6% in FY2025 [D218][D311][D406].
The FY2017 operating margin of -422.5% followed a $2.6 billion rise in stock-based compensation tied to the CEO award and IPO-triggered RSUs [F22][P74][X82].

In FY2022 operating margin fell 13.3pp to -30.3% as operating expenses grew 24.4% against revenue growth of 11.8%, and the filing attributes the weaker Adjusted EBITDA to higher cost of revenue and overall operating expenses [D276][F27][D280][D263][P42].
FY2025 revenue rose 10.6%, with advertising contributing 5.3pp and Other Revenue 5.4pp [D406][D538][D545].
The filing ties the advertising gain to roughly 17% more impressions, partly offset by roughly 10% lower price per impression, and the Other Revenue gain to more subscribers [P24].
Advertising was 87.4% of FY2025 revenue, down from 95.7% in FY2023, while Other Revenue reached 12.6% [D536][D532][D543].
The FY2025 incremental operating margin was 44.8%, and revenue growth exceeded operating-cost growth by 5.5pp [D429][D430].
The net loss narrowed 34.0% in FY2025, while diluted shares rose 2.1% to 1,694.6 million [D408][D425][X150].
FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% is the window high, against a median of -32.4% and a low of -422.5% [F30][D554][D555][D553].
The FY2025 gain of 5.7pp came from cost of revenue (+1.1pp), R&D (+1.3pp) and other lines (+3.3pp) [D419][D431][D432][D433].
Sales and marketing fell $42.4 million on the timing of prior-year marketing events and lower advertising investment [P22].
The largest window move was FY2018 at +315.1pp, after stock-based compensation expense fell $2.1 billion [D92][P75].

Net margin of -7.8% was helped by $68.9 million of other income, driven by $96.7 million of debt extinguishment gains, while interest expense reached $122.0 million on the 2033 and 2034 Notes [F50][X130][P18][X100][P19].
Operating cash flow of $656.2 million and free cash flow of $437.2 million contrast with a $460.5 million net loss [F80][F100][F40].
The filing attributes operating cash flow to the net loss adjusted for non-cash items, including $1.0 billion of stock-based compensation [P13][X90].
Free cash flow margin was 7.4%, against a window median of -4.1% [D393][D561].
Capex of $219.0 million was 3.7% of revenue and 1.34x D&A [F90][D392][D395].
Cash and investments of $2,940.6 million against debt of $3,536.8 million left net debt of $596.3 million, up from $267.6 million in FY2024 [D397][D398][D399][D351].
Net cash was -10.1% of revenue, in the 0th percentile of five internet peers whose median is 45.0% [D400][D578][D579].
The current ratio of 3.56x is the window low, though it still sits above 1x [F180][D565].
Buybacks of $750.9 million were 171.7% of free cash flow [X156][D402].
Diluted shares still rose 2.1% in FY2025 [D425].
R1: Snap has posted a net loss in each of 10 years, including $460.5 million in FY2025 [R1][F40].
The loss is narrowing, but the operating margin remains in the 0th percentile of five internet peers, whose median is 20.3% [D570][D571].
R2: Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue and 191.1% of the operating loss in FY2025 [R2][D390][D404].
Without that non-cash expense the loss would be far smaller, so dilution is the real cost of the improvement.
R3: Net cash has fallen four years running into net debt, reaching $596.3 million in FY2025 [R3][D399].
R4: Buybacks exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 [R4][D307][D354][D402].
Returns above free cash flow are being funded from the balance sheet, and the filings cited do not say how long that will continue.
Free cash flow margin falling below the FY2024 level of 4.1% would reverse the improvement from the FY2025 level of 7.4% [D345][D393]; this will appear in the FY2026 10-K.
Operating margin worsening past -14.7%, the FY2024 level, would undo the FY2025 gain to -9.0% [F29][F30]; this will appear in the FY2026 10-K.
Net debt widening beyond $596.3 million would extend the four-year slide [D399]; this will appear in the FY2026 10-K.
Other Revenue growth dropping below FY2025's 62.9% pace would test its role as the second growth driver [D544]; this will appear in the FY2026 10-K.
